t: In front of you is the statue of Lord George Bentinck, at the southern end of Cavendish Square in Marylebone. It's Grade II listed. Bentinck was a Conservative politician and racehorse owner, noted for his role in unseating Sir Robert Peel over the Corn Laws. The statue was made by Thomas Campbell, a Scottish sculptor of the early 19th century. He is most notable for his statue of Sarah Siddons in Westminster Abbey, and he was heavily patronised by the British aristocracy.
